title: Advice for Youth
paragraphs: Dalam sebuah surat yang ditulis untuk cucunya sebelum memulai kuliah, seorang sesepuh merenungkan pilihan-pilihan yang telah membentuk hidupnya sendiri, berharap pengalamannya dapat menghindarkan cucunya dari kesulitan yang tidak perlu.

Ia menulis bahwa jika ia memahami lebih awal betapa pentingnya kesabaran dibanding bakat mentah, ia akan jauh lebih sedikit khawatir membandingkan dirinya terus-menerus dengan teman sekelas yang lebih berbakat secara alami.

Surat itu juga membahas persahabatan secara langsung, memperingatkan bahwa jika cucunya memilih teman secara sembarangan, ia kemungkinan akan mendapati karakternya sendiri secara bertahap dibentuk oleh kebiasaan yang tidak pernah sengaja ia adopsi.

Yang mungkin paling penting, sesepuh itu menekankan bahwa jika cucunya tetap menjaga shalat hariannya bahkan selama masa ujian tersibuk, ia akan mendapati shalat itu menjadi penopangnya alih-alih mengalihkan perhatiannya.

Surat itu ditutup dengan pengakuan bahwa kesalahan tidak terhindarkan selama tahun-tahun pembentukan ini, tapi mendesak cucunya untuk memandang setiap kesalahan sebagai informasi berharga alih-alih bukti kegagalan permanen.

Bertahun-tahun kemudian, sang cucu menyimpan surat ini dan membacanya kembali selama momen-momen sulitnya sendiri, mengatakan surat itu terus menawarkan bimbingan jauh setelah tantangan spesifik yang awalnya dibahasnya telah berlalu.
answerKey: In a letter written to his grandson before starting university, an elder reflected on the choices that had shaped his own life, hoping his experience might spare his grandson some unnecessary difficulty. He wrote that if he had understood earlier how much patience mattered more than raw talent, he would have worried far less about comparing himself constantly to more naturally gifted classmates. The letter also addressed friendship directly, warning that if his grandson chose companions carelessly, he would likely find his own character gradually shaped by habits he never consciously intended to adopt. Perhaps most significantly, the elder emphasized that if his grandson maintained his daily prayers even during his busiest exam periods, he would find they anchored him rather than distracted him. The letter closed by acknowledging that mistakes were inevitable during these formative years, but urged his grandson to view each mistake as valuable information rather than evidence of some permanent failure. Years later, the grandson kept this letter and has reread it during his own difficult moments, saying it continues to offer guidance long after the specific challenges it originally addressed had passed.
